record.paper_title: Stationary solutions of the axially symmetric Einstein-Vlasov system: present status and open problems
record.original_question: Can regular stationary Einstein-Vlasov solutions with ergoregions be constructed beyond the known highly rotating step-function ansatz family, in particular with total angular momentum |J| below the squared mass M² or using non-step-function ansatzes for particle energy and axial angular momentum? Here an ergoregion is the region where the stationary time-translation Killing field ∂t becomes spacelike, equivalently in the metric parametrization e^(2ν) − ρ²B²ω²e^(−2ν) < 0.

evidence.quote: The definition of an ergoregion is that the Killing field ∂t which corresponds to the time translation symmetry becomes spacelike.
In our parametrization of the metric it follows that an ergoregion is the set for which e2ν − ρ2B2ω2e−2ν < 0.
The solutions admitting ergoregions that we obtain are all highly relativistic and highly rotating, each satisfying the inequality |J | > M2.
Perhaps a different numerical scheme will be more successful in finding solutions with ergoregions and with |J | < M2.
It would be interesting to look for ergoregions in families of solutions obtained from other (non-step function) ansatzes.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the stationary, axially symmetric Einstein–Vlasov system on a four-dimensional spacetime equipped with two commuting Killing vector fields: the time-translation $\partial_t$ and the axial rotation $\partial_\varphi$. In quasi-isotropic coordinates $(t,\rho,z,\varphi)$ the metric is written as
$$ds^2 = -e^{2\nu}dt^2 + e^{2\mu}(d\rho^2+dz^2) + \rho^2 B^2 e^{-2\nu}(d\varphi - \omega\, dt)^2,$$
where $\nu,\mu,B,\omega$ are functions of $(\rho,z)$ only. The matter is described by a nonnegative phase-space distribution function $f$ satisfying the Vlasov equation, with stress-energy tensor sourcing the Einstein equations. By the Killing symmetries, the particle energy $E = -g(\partial_t,p)$ and axial angular momentum $L = g(\partial_\varphi,p)$ are conserved along geodesics, so one customarily takes $f = \Phi(E,L)$ for some ansatz function $\Phi$. The total ADM mass $M$ and total angular momentum $J$ are well-defined asymptotic quantities for asymptotically flat solutions.

An ergoregion is the open set where $\partial_t$ becomes spacelike, equivalently the set on which
$$e^{2\nu} - \rho^2 B^2 \omega^2 e^{-2\nu} < 0.$$

The only currently known regular stationary asymptotically flat solutions of the axially symmetric Einstein–Vlasov system that possess an ergoregion are obtained using a step-function (cutoff) ansatz of the form $\Phi(E,L) = (E_0 - E)_+^k\, \mathbf{1}_{\{L \geq L_0\}}$ (or similar step-function dependence in $L$), and all such solutions are highly rotating, in particular satisfying $|J| > M^2$.

Problem. Construct regular stationary asymptotically flat solutions of the axially symmetric Einstein–Vlasov system that possess an ergoregion and that satisfy at least one of:
(a) $|J| < M^2$;
(b) the ansatz $\Phi(E,L)$ is not of step-function type in $L$ (e.g., smooth in $L$).
Equivalently, prove existence (or non-existence) of such solutions.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent surveys of stationary axially symmetric Einstein-Vlasov solutions describe the construction of solutions with ergoregions only via a highly rotating step-function ansatz, all satisfying |J|>M². The status report explicitly lists the construction of solutions with ergoregions and |J|<M² (or via non-step-function ansatzes) as an unresolved problem, suggesting that different numerical schemes or analytical methods may be needed. No subsequent work was found resolving it.

status_evidence.title: Stationary solutions of the axially symmetric Einstein-Vlasov system: present status and open problems
status_evidence.snippet: Solutions admitting ergoregions are highly relativistic and highly rotating with |J|>M²; obtaining solutions with ergoregions and |J|<M² remains open.
status_evidence.claim: Listed as an open problem in the current status review.

status_evidence.title: The Einstein-Vlasov System/Kinetic Theory (Living Reviews)
status_evidence.snippet: Surveys existence results for stationary axisymmetric Einstein-Vlasov solutions; ergoregion solutions outside step-function families not established.
status_evidence.claim: No general existence result for non-step-function ansatz solutions with ergoregions is recorded.
